post.author: TDengine
post.topic_summary: Jeff Tao and Jeff Winter discuss moving from collecting more data to making industrial data actionable in the AI era, covering why teams struggle to bridge that gap.

comment_posted.comment_text:
The jump from collecting to actionable is almost always a normalization problem, not a volume problem. Historians store the time series but not the semantics: you have the value but no context for what it means (which machine, which operation, what normal looks like, what a deviation means). So when AI is pointed at raw historian data, it generates plausible-looking answers that are wrong because the context is not there.

The practical fix is a semantic layer between the historian and the AI context window: normalized schemas, equipment models, named operations. Once the AI can ask 'what is OEE for this machine this shift' and get a structured answer rather than 600 raw time-series points, it starts producing answers that are actually actionable.

That intermediate layer is the part most teams skip because the raw data pipeline is already hard enough.
